text:
Maria Chen: Heads-up — architecture question for the private metrics gateway we ship with the on‑prem agent. We need a small, auditable handshake that works with restrictive firewalls + customer KMS. What should the protocol and ports look like?

Jamal Singh: My vote: mTLS handshake on 8443 for the persistent channel. Agent initiates TLS, we validate client cert. For customers who don't want cert import, support JWTs signed by customer KMS as fallback.

Oskar Petrov: +1 but we should avoid asking customers to upload long-lived certs. Proposal: ephemeral client certs minted by customer KMS or Redwood intermediary. Flow: agent -> POST /v1/handshake (TLS 8443) with KMS-signed JWT; server returns temporary client cert and upload/ws endpoint. Example handshake (pseudo):

```bash
curl -X POST https://metrics-gateway.private.redwood:8443/v1/handshake \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"kid":"projects/abc/keys/xyz","jwt":"<signed_jwt>","agent_id":"agent-42"}'

# 200 -> {"client_cert":"-----BEGIN CERT...","ingest_url":"wss://...:8443/stream"}
```

Nadia Lopez: From the firewall side customers will only open outbound to a few hosts. Recommend we publish a small IP set + DNS name. Minimum ports: 443 (fallback HTTPS) and 8443 (mTLS websocket). Example ACLs:
- outbound TCP 8443 to metrics-gateway.private.redwood.example:8443
- outbound TCP 443 to metrics-upload.redwood.example:443 (S3-style fallback)
- allow ephemeral UDP/TCP ephemeral ports for websocket TLS handshake (normal behavior)

DevOps Bot: Telemetry contract (fields we need in the initial MVP):
- metric_names: ["inference.requests.total", "inference.latency.p50_ms", "inference.latency.p95_ms", "exporter.bytes_sent", "exporter.batches", "agent.connection.uptime"]
- required_labels: ["tenant_id","agent_id","region","model_variant"]
- optional: ["batch_size","kv_cache_hit_rate"]

Jamal Singh: Quotas & routing: if agent pushes to our hosted collector we need per-tenant token accounting. If they push to customer S3 we only ingest metadata. Also: routing policy — try mTLS gateway first, if unreachable fall back to HTTPS multipart upload to S3 endpoint. That keeps latency low for streaming workloads and still works behind strict proxies.

Maria Chen: UX asks for the console: we need a dashboard template that maps runtime labels to charts automatically (tenant -> agent -> model_variant). Also a rollout UX: allow admin to route X% of agents to hosted collector for canary and visual diff. Dashboards should show bytes_sent, request_rate, and connection errors in one pane.

Oskar Petrov: Audit log hooks: every handshake must emit an audit event with fields {event: "handshake", agent_id, tenant_id, signed_token_id, client_cert_fingerprint, exporter_ip}. We should support two modes: 1) forward audit events to customer SIEM via webhook, 2) store in Redwood audit bucket (customer-controlled retention).

Nadia Lopez: Ops constraints: we'll need a ready-made firewall checklist for customers and a small NAT/egress test script. Also ensure mutual TLS cert expiry>renewal by KMS rotation.

Maria Chen: Action items I see: 1) eng-platform: publish firewall + port/IP doc (Nadia) 2) eng-runtime: draft /v1/handshake proto + example (Oskar) 3) eng-console: dashboard template + canary routing UI spec (me) 4) infra: define telemetry schema + quota accounting changes (Jamal) 5) sec: review KMS signing flow and token TTL (security review ticket). I'll open PRs for the doc + spec by EOD Friday.

Jamal Singh: I'll add a unit test harness that simulates failed handshake -> fallback path. Also will add metrics: handshake.success, handshake.duration_ms, handshake.failure_reason (label).

Oskar Petrov: I'll start the handshake API PR, include example responses for both cert issuance and S3 fallback token. Might push a WIP by tomorrow.

DevOps Bot: Noted. Created ticket INF-4821 to track telemetry contract changes and dashboard mapping.

Maria Chen: Thanks — ping me on the PRs @Jamal @Oskar. If customers ask for only outbound to a single DNS name we should support that with an HTTPS-only small-batch uploader. :thumbsup:
